knowledge:
- key_parameters: ratio=Cutoff ratio (e.g. 0.33) in makeBaseCalls to determine if a peak is signal or noise ;; string=Logical (TRUE/FALSE) in primarySeq/secondarySeq to return sequence as character string or DNAString ;; width=Number of bases per row in chromatogram ;; height=Height of each row in chromatogram ;; trim5=Number of bases to trim from the 5' end in chromatogram or setAllelePhase ;; trim3=Number of bases to trim from the 3' end in chromatogram or setAllelePhase ;; showcalls=Determines which basecalls to show in chromatogram ("primary", "secondary", or "both")
- alternatives: read.abif and read.scf are low-level alternatives to readsangerseq, preferred only when direct inspection of raw file fields is required ;; PolyPeakParser() is a local web application alternative included in the package for users who prefer a graphical user interface to automate heterozygous indel separation
- when_to_use: When analyzing Sanger sequencing data (ABIF or SCF formats) to resolve heterozygous indels, make secondary basecalls, or phase alleles against a reference sequence
- pitfalls: chromatogram() can throw an error if the graphics device dimensions are not large enough, so users should save to a PDF file to automatically size it ;; Secondary basecalls in raw .ab1 files can be inconsistent or contain noise, so makeBaseCalls should be used with an appropriate ratio cutoff to filter noise ;; SCF files are unable to show secondary basecalls natively

workflows.name: sanger_sequencing_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze Sanger sequencing chromatograms to make basecalls, phase alleles against a reference, and align the resulting sequences.
input: heterozygous.ab1 (Sanger sequencing chromatogram file in ABIF format)
homozygous.scf (Sanger sequencing chromatogram file in SCF format, used here as reference)
workflows.stages: 1. Load chromatogram data using readsangerseq or read.scf/sangerseq ;; 2. Extract and manipulate sequences using primarySeq ;; 3. Plot chromatograms using chromatogram ;; 4. Make primary and secondary basecalls using makeBaseCalls ;; 5. Phase alleles against a reference sequence using setAllelePhase ;; 6. Align and compare phased alleles using pairwiseAlignment and writePairwiseAlignments
workflows.code:
hetab1 <- read.abif(system.file("extdata", 
                                "heterozygous.ab1", 
                                package="sangerseqR"))
homoscf <- read.scf(system.file("extdata", 
                                "homozygous.scf", 
                                package="sangerseqR"))
homosangerseq <- sangerseq(homoscf)
hetsangerseq <- readsangerseq(system.file("extdata", 
                                          "heterozygous.ab1", 
                                          package="sangerseqR"))
Seq1 <- primarySeq(homosangerseq)
reverseComplement(Seq1)
primarySeq(homosangerseq, string=TRUE)
chromatogram(hetsangerseq, width=80, height=3, trim5=50, trim3=100, 
             showcalls='both')
hetcalls <- makeBaseCalls(hetsangerseq, ratio=0.33)
chromatogram(hetcalls, width=80, height=3, trim5=50, trim3=100, 
             showcalls='both')
ref <- subseq(primarySeq(homosangerseq, string=TRUE), start=30, width=500)
hetseqalleles <- setAllelePhase(hetcalls, ref, trim5=50, trim3=300)
pa <- pairwiseAlignment(primarySeq(hetseqalleles)[1:400], 
                        secondarySeq(hetseqalleles)[1:400], 
                        type="global-local")
writePairwiseAlignments(pa)
